stories.headline: ‘Fresh proposal for more LoC bunkers sent to Centre’
stories.title: ‘Fresh proposal for more LoC bunkers sent to Centre’
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 25: The Jammu and Kashmir government has submitted a fresh proposal to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs for construction of additional bunkers along the Line of Control (LoC), with the proposal at an advanced stage of consideration, Chief Secretary Dr Sajjan Singh Yadav said on Wednesday. The Chief Secretary was interacting with residents during a Block Diwas-cum-public grievances redressal camp at Bhawani, a vibrant village in Nowshera block of Rajouri district, where residents raised the demand for additional underground bunkers to protect civilians in border areas. Responding to the demand, Yadav said: "A fresh proposal had been submitted to the Ministry of Home Affairs and was at an advanced stage of consideration." Official figures show that 2,783 underground bunkers have already been constructed for civilian safety along the LoC in Rajouri district. "Of these, 1,528 were built by the Rural Development Department, while the Public Works Department constructed 1,255 bunkers," the figures suggest. The demand for additional protective infrastructure has gained significance following intense Pakistani shelling and drone attacks on forward villages during Operation Sindoor in May 2025. The attacks left 27 people, mostly civilians, dead and around 70 injured in Jammu and Kashmir. Jammu and Kashmir shares a 221-kilometre International Border with Pakistan across Kathua, Samba and Jammu districts, while the Line of Control stretches for approximately 744 kilometres, making civilian safety and protective infrastructure major priorities for border communities. During the public interaction, residents also raised several developmental demands, including granting shrine status to Maa Mangla Mata Temple, organising a border tourism mela, double-laning of the Nowshera-Jhangar road, filling vacancies in educational institutions and establishing a sports stadium at Kalsian. The residents also sought improved healthcare facilities, including a dispensary and ambulance service for Bhawani. Assuring the people that their demands would be examined by the concerned departments, the Chief Secretary directed the Rajouri Deputy Commissioner to prepare a comprehensive development plan for Maa Mangla Mata Shrine, keeping in view its religious significance and tourism potential. On the shortage of teaching staff in border schools, he said the matter would be taken up with the Education Department. He also asked the Deputy Commissioner (DC) to identify suitable land for the proposed sports stadium at Kalsian and explore the possibility of developing indoor sports facilities in schools with higher student enrolment. Yadav said appropriate measures would be explored to provide a dispensary and ambulance services in Bhawani. The demand for establishing a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the area would also be taken up, he added. Emphasising economic opportunities in border villages, the Chief Secretary encouraged local youth to explore entrepreneurship, skill development and startup initiatives to strengthen the socio-economic development of these areas. He directed officials to sensitise residents about collateral-free loans, startup financing and other government support schemes. During the programme, Yadav distributed sanction letters among beneficiaries under the Holistic Agriculture Development Programme and Sheep Husbandry schemes. He also handed over engagement orders to newly appointed Anganwadi workers.

stories.headline: Sheshnag safe: Forest Minister
stories.title: Sheshnag safe: Forest Minister
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 25: Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister Altaf Ahmad Kaloo on Wednesday said maintenance work on the Amarnath Yatra track had caused no damage to Sheshnag Lake, accusing the People's Democratic Party (PDP) of helping the Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) politicise the issue ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections. Kaloo said a 12-member team inspected the site on Tuesday on the directions of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and found no damage to the alpine lake. “A team was sent to the spot yesterday on the directions of the Chief Minister. Later, I was apprised by the officials that Sheshnag Lake is completely safe. The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) has not done anything to the lake. The viral video is misleading, as there is a gap of 200-300 feet between the yatra track and the lake. It is a sacred religious place for our Hindu brethren, Muslims as well as Sikhs,” Kaloo said addressing a news conference at the Pahalgam Club and Convention Centre. Sharing fresh video footage of the site, the minister said, “This is Sheshnag as it stands today. Nothing has been done to Sheshnag. Not a single speck of earth has entered the lake.” He said the inspection team included officials from the Environment, Ecology and Territorial Forest divisions and the Forest Protection Force (FPF). Defending the BRO, Kaloo referred to the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed between Chief Minister Omar Abdullah-led government and BRO’s Project Beacon in 2025 for maintenance of the Amarnath Yatra track. “An unfortunate eventuality occurred in 2012 along the trek. The Supreme Court, while taking cognisance of it, ordered a 12-foot trek -six feet for pilgrims proceeding to the cave shrine and six more for those returning. The current track is in accordance with the Supreme Court ruling,” he said. Kaloo said maintenance work on the track had been undertaken after the yatra in 2022 and repairs were carried out every year before and after the yatra to fix damaged tiles, edges, and other portions. “We are checking all the parameters of the MoU to ensure they are followed. I wanted to visit the lake but couldn’t due to security reasons. I was told there was no security ahead,” he said. Accusing the PDP of helping the BJP politicise the issue, Kaloo said the two parties were “making a mountain out of a molehill” to create a political issue for the Uttar Pradesh elections. National Conference MLA and party's chief spokesman Tanvir Sadiq said Chief Minister Omar Abdullah had taken cognisance of the video circulating on social media and sought a report from the Forest Minister. The controversy erupted earlier this week after a video posted by a JCB operator on social media showed a crawler excavator being used for track maintenance near the lake, triggering concerns over construction activity in the fragile Himalayan region. On Tuesday, PDP President Mehbooba Mufti attempted to visit Sheshnag but was stopped by police at Chandanwari in Pahalgam. Police cited security concerns and did not allow her to proceed further. The video had drawn criticism from political leaders, religious figures and environmentalists, who raised concerns over the ecological impact of the work near the alpine lake. Situated at an altitude of 12,100 feet along the route to the Amarnath Cave, Sheshnag Lake is among the 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified across Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.headline: Supreme Court's Sabarimala verdict due before Christmas; Knanaya endogamy case deferred as ruling may have a bearing
stories.title: Supreme Court's Sabarimala verdict due before Christmas; Knanaya endogamy case deferred as ruling may have a bearing
stories.summary: The Supreme Court indicated that the Sabarimala reference verdict could come before the Christmas break and deferred the Knanaya Church’s endogamy case to January 2027.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Kasaragod: The Supreme Court on Wednesday indicated that its verdict in the Sabarimala reference on women's entry into the hill shrine would be delivered before the Christmas break.

The indication came while the apex court was hearing a challenge by the Knanaya Catholic Church against a Kerala High Court judgment that struck down the Church's practice of enforcing endogamy by excluding members who marry outside the community.
The Bench deferred the Knanaya petitions, observing that the Sabarimala ruling could have a bearing on the issues involved.

A three-judge Bench of Justices B V Nagarathna, R Mahadevan and Sanjeev Sachdeva deferred the Knanaya petitions to January 5, 2027, indicating that they would be considered after the nine-judge Constitution Bench delivers its verdict in the Sabarimala reference.

Justice B V Nagarathna said that the Sabarimala verdict was likely to be delivered before the Supreme Court closes for its Christmas vacation on December 18, Adv Sai Shashank, who represents the reformist group in the Knanaya case, told Onmanorama.
The nine-judge Bench had reserved its judgment on May 14 after 16 days of hearings.
The Sabarimala reference, however, goes beyond the question of women’s entry into the hill shrine.
Several other disputes involving religious practices and the rights of religious denominations have been tagged with the reference for consideration by the larger Bench, said Adv Shashank.

These include challenges concerning the entry of Muslim women into mosques and dargahs, the exclusion of Parsi women from fire temples after marrying outside the community, and the practice of female genital mutilation among the Dawoodi Bohra community.
The reference also encompasses the Dawoodi Bohra community’s power to excommunicate members, he said.

The larger Bench is examining constitutional questions on the scope of religious freedom under Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution, the autonomy of religious denominations, the limits of judicial scrutiny of religious practices and the relationship between individual rights and denominational rights.

The Knanaya dispute raises a closely related question: whether a religious community can invoke its right to manage its own affairs to enforce endogamy, or whether an individual’s right to choose a spouse takes precedence.

stories.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
stories.summary: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh.
A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6.
The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided.
Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government.
The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders.
“And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally.
The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions.
The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30.
The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute.
The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls.
As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144.

A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise.

stories.headline: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
stories.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for over 42 lakh farmers
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for over 42.30 lakh farmers not covered under Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), a ₹5,548-crore provision for the Narmada-Tapi diversion project in Nandurbar, confiscation of assets of firms involved in financial fraud, and a law to regulate private-aided schools, among 14 decisions.

At the meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, the Cabinet decided to give free foodgrains to farmers who are not covered under the National Food Security Act in 33 drought-affected districts of the State.
The beneficiaries belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.
“The farmers will receive five kg of foodgrains per person every month, free of cost, for the next three months.
This will include three kg rice and two kg wheat,” stated a release issued from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).
With an aim to strengthen the irrigation system in Nandurbar district, the Cabinet gave nod to the Narmada-Tapi diversion project.
This will include six diversions weirs that aim to benefit around 26,526 hectares with irrigation while generating 11.50 MW power, as per the Water Resources Department officials.
The Maharashtra government has also approved the plan to set up a separate MPID (Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors) tribunal with a time limit of 90 days for the disposal of cases.
The Cabinet also decided to expedite the process of confiscating properties of institutions committing financial fraud and amend the MPID Act,” stated the CMO.

The State government has also decided to increase the hostel allowances for students from Economically Weaker Sections (EBC, SEBC and EWS) pursuing professional degree courses in health sciences under the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme.
It also approved the provision of financial facilities for teachers through RBI-registered institutions.
The Cabinet approved the draft Maharashtra Private-Aided Schools (Regulation) Bill, 2026, which will be tabled in the legislature.

The Maharashtra government has also approved the plan to set up a separate MPID (Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors) tribunal with a time limit of 90 days for the disposal of cases.
The Cabinet also decided to expedite the process of confiscating properties of institutions committing financial fraud and amend the MPID Act,” stated the CMO.

The State government has also decided to increase the hostel allowances for students from Economically Weaker Sections (EBC, SEBC and EWS) pursuing professional degree courses in health sciences under the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance Scheme.

stories.headline: 'No structural excess capacity in any sector': India pushes back against US tariff allegations
stories.title: 'No structural excess capacity in any sector': India pushes back against US tariff allegations
stories.summary: India said on Wednesday that it remained committed to concluding a bilateral trade agreement with the US at the earliest.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: “Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation...,” the Indian government said in a statement, adding that the notice was “currently under examination.”
“India engaged constructively throughout this investigation.
In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector,” the statement said.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced on Wednesday that tariffs on Indian imports would be capped at 17 per cent if the two countries reached a trade agreement.
In the absence of a deal, the tariffs would increase to 25 per cent.
The Indian government reiterated its commitment to finalising the proposed agreement.

“Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026, and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026,” it said.
During its negotiations with the US, India has been seeking a competitive advantage over its Asian rivals.
Washington has addressed this demand in its tariff proposals.

The Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) said the Section 301 excess-capacity investigations recreated the reciprocal-tariff regime under a new name and were designed to push trading partners into signing one-sided and expensive trade agreements rather than addressing structural industrial overproduction, according to a PTI report.
GTRI said Washington's dual-rate structure threatened steep baseline tariffs against countries that refused an agreement while offering lower rates to those that signed one.

According to the organisation, the structure allowed Washington to regain bargaining power to impose duties and seek unilateral concessions, enabling a government to secure tariff relief even if the industrial capacity that prompted the investigation remained unchanged.
